references.text: The Philistines envy Isaac because of his wealth, and Abimelek asks Isaac to leave. This is the direct background for Isaac's question in verse 27 about why they seek him out after having shown hostility.
Abraham confronts Abimelek regarding a well that Abimelek's servants had taken by force. This shows tension from a previous generation with the same king/people, which repeats itself in Isaac's time.
The story of Abraham's conflict with Abimelek over Sarah shows a conflict from a previous generation with the same people, which may have contributed to the strained relationship.
Jephthah asks a very similar question to the elders of Gilead: 'Was it not you who hated me and drove me away? Why do you come to me now when you are in trouble?' A close parallel to Isaac's words.
Disputes over the wells Esek and Sitna show the ongoing hostility from the Philistines that Isaac refers to in verse 27.
